questions.question: Explosive materials are usually put in which hazard class?
questions.explanation: Class 1 materials can cause explosions or fires.

questions.question: What must the shipper include in emergency response information?

options.text: How many people should respond in an accident.

questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include fire and explosion risks, material names, health hazards, precautions for accidents, how to handle fires, how to handle spills, and basic first aid.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, what should you check about emergency exits?

options.text: That they are difficult to open.
That they cannot be opened from inside the cab.

questions.explanation: Check that emergency exit warning devices work properly. All exits should open easily, have no damage, and close securely from inside.

questions.question: What material should the floor liner be made of when transporting Division 1.1 materials?
questions.explanation: The floor liner must be tight and made from non-metallic material or metal without iron.

questions.question: Who puts placards on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: The shipper provides the placards, but the driver is responsible for placing them on the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do before opening the filling hole on a tank with flammable liquids?

options.text: Break the ground right before opening the hole.
Lock the filling hole during loading.

questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading. Ground the tank before opening the filling hole and keep it grounded until after closing the hole.

questions.question: If a vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives is in a collision, what should the driver do?

options.text: Not warn others about the danger.
Leave the explosives in the vehicle while separating it from the other vehicle.
Remove the explosives before separating the vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the explosives before separating the vehicles.
questions.explanation: Warn others of danger and keep people away. Do not allow smoking or fires. Remove all explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and buildings before separating the vehicles.

questions.question: What is NOT required of a person supervising tank loading or unloading?

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
Know the hazards of the materials.

questions.explanation: The supervisor must be alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank. A chemical suit is not required.

questions.question: What should you check about the pedals during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: That the surface is smoothed out.
That something is under the brake pedal.

questions.explanation: Make sure nothing is under or around the pedals that would prevent them from working. Check that the pedals work properly and have grooved surfaces if applicable.

questions.question: How many hazardous materials classes exist?
questions.explanation: There are nine hazardous materials classes. Each class represents the risks linked to that type of material.

questions.question: What must be in a vehicle that is transporting chlorine?
questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must have an approved gas mask in the vehicle. They must also have an emergency kit to control leaks in the cargo tank fittings.

questions.question: Many poisonous products are also:
questions.explanation: Many poisonous products are also flammable. Take the right safety steps if you think your cargo might be flammable.

questions.question: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify that the package:

options.text: Has been prepared following all rules.
Was packed at a specific location.
Will be placed on the trailer first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has been prepared following all rules.
questions.explanation: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they confirm that the package has been prepared according to all required rules.

questions.question: When a driver is not in the vehicle, hazardous materials shipping papers should be:
questions.explanation: Shipping papers for hazardous materials must be easy to find. When the driver is not in the vehicle, leave the papers on the driver's seat.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading a tank with flammable liquids. The only exception is if the engine needs to run to operate a pump.

questions.question: A person loading a tank with hazardous materials must be all of the following, except:

options.text: Aware of the hazards of the materials.

questions.explanation: The supervisor of loading or unloading must be alert, able to see the tank, within 25 feet of the tank, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be authorized to move the tank.

questions.question: The identification number for a hazardous material should appear:

options.text: On a bumper sticker on the vehicle.

questions.explanation: The material's ID number must appear on the shipping paper and on the packaging. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other bulk containers.

questions.question: Your engine runs a pump during delivery of compressed gas. After delivery, turn off the engine ____ unhooking the hoses.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine when loading or unloading a compressed gas tank unless the engine runs a pump. If the engine runs a pump, turn it off after the product transfer but before unhooking the hoses.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts must be all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, all lug nuts must be present, free of cracks and distortions, and not loose. Check for rust trails or shiny threads that show looseness. All bolt holes must also be free of cracks and distortions.

questions.question: What could show that a shipment you are accepting contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is packaged in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often contain hazardous materials. Take the right safety steps if you are transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: Containers of hazardous materials must be:

options.text: Secured so they do not move during transport.
A maximum of four feet tall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so they do not move during transport.
questions.explanation: Hazardous material containers must be secured so they will not fall, slide, or bounce around while being transported.

questions.question: Shippers must label hazardous materials. If an item is too small for its label, how should you label it?

options.text: Tie the item with other hazardous materials and put a label sheet on the outside of the bundle.
Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
Mark the item with a large orange dot.
Place the item in a box with a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped hazard labels must go on most hazardous material packages. If the label does not fit on the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: ____ identical placards must be placed on a vehicle transporting hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: When hazardous materials placards are required, place them on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: When checking the springs during a vehicle inspection, do all of the following, except:

options.text: Check that torsion springs are not damaged.

questions.explanation: During spring inspection, look for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs and broken or distorted coil springs. Check that torsion bars, torque arms, and other suspension parts are not damaged and are mounted securely. Do not glue cracked springs.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: The vehicle crossing over an exercise boundary line.
A driver executing a single pull-up.
A driver putting the vehicle in neutral and applying the parking brake.
The vehicle stalling while shifting gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle crossing over an exercise boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment is when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses an exercise boundary line. Every encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: During the on-road driving skills test, you are evaluated on gear usage. You should not:

options.text: Select a gear that makes the engine work too hard.
Forget to shift through an intersection.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, select a gear that does not make the engine work too hard or too softly. Avoid grinding gears. Do not shift gears while turning or crossing through intersections.

questions.question: Which agency helps coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards?

options.text: The United Center for Chemical Assistance

questions.explanation: The National Response Center helps police and firefighters coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When checking the air and electrical lines during a vehicle inspection, all of the following should be true, except:

options.text: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
The air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
The air lines are not pinched.
The air lines are not dragging against tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: When checking air and electrical lines, listen for leaks. Make sure the hoses and lines are not cut, chafed, spliced, or worn. Ensure they are not tangled, pinched, or dragging against tractor parts.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.

questions.explanation: For your CDL, you must pass a vehicle inspection test. Walk around the vehicle and point to or touch each item. Explain to the examiner what you are checking and why. You do not need to crawl under the vehicle or hood.
